definitions.explanation: Individual words or short expressions in a text.

examples.japanese: {語句|ごく}の{意味|いみ}を{調|しら}べる。
examples.english: To look up the meaning of words.

examples.japanese: {論文|ろんぶん}を{書|か}く{際|さい}は、{適切|てきせつ}な{語句|ごく}を{選|えら}ぶことが{重要|じゅうよう}だ。
examples.english: When writing a paper, it's important to choose appropriate wording.

examples.japanese: {英語|えいご}の{教科書|きょうかしょ}に{出|で}てくる{語句|ごく}を{一|ひと}つずつ{覚|おぼ}えていった。
examples.english: I memorized the words and phrases from the English textbook one by one.

notes:
{語句|ごく} refers to words and short phrases, especially in the context of reading, studying, or writing. It is composed of {語|ご} (word) + {句|く} (phrase/clause).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {語句|ごく}の{意味|いみ}: meaning of words/phrases
- {語句|ごく}を{調|しら}べる: to look up words
- {語句|ごく}を{覚|おぼ}える: to memorize vocabulary
- {適切|てきせつ}な{語句|ごく}: appropriate wording

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {単語|たんご}: an individual word (the most common term for "word")
- {語彙|ごい}: vocabulary (a collective set of words)
- {表現|ひょうげん}: expression (broader, includes sentence-level phrasing)
- {用語|ようご}: technical term, terminology

{語句|ごく} is somewhat formal and often appears in academic or literary contexts. In everyday conversation, {単語|たんご} or {言葉|ことば} is more natural.

HOMOPHONE:
Do not confuse with ごく ({極|ごく}, extremely), which is an adverb.
